title: The NBA’s Possession-Maxxers Are Having It Both Ways
contentHtml:
Last weekend, I read something really interesting by , one of my favorite fellow data-analysts/chart-makers:

The basic premise is that NBA teams are currently engaging in “possession-maxxing,” or maximizing the number of extra plays they create through grabbing more rebounds and having fewer turnovers than the opponent. Lev found that leaguewide offensive rebounding and turnover-forcing are both at recent high-water marks, and that winning the shot-attempt margin — a natural consequence of grabbing more boards and winning the turnover battle — has exploded in its correlation with winning ballgames.

But when I dug into the same numbers myself, I found another intriguing wrinkle: For most of the past two decades, the teams getting more shots tended to be the ones scoring less efficiently. Lately, that relationship has flipped, and it might help explain why winning the shot-attempt battle suddenly matters so much more.
